opportunities.title: Opportunity marketplace
opportunities.purpose: Short stretch assignments matched to your skills: projects, outage support, shadowing, OE reviews, knowledge capture, outreach and research.

opportunities-my.title: My opportunities
opportunities-my.purpose: Track your applications from line-manager release to sign-off, and the skills evidence they add to your passport.

opportunities-manage.title: Release and selection desk
opportunities-manage.purpose: Release your people for stretch work, select applicants for your postings and sign off outcomes.

opportunities-post.title: Post an opportunity
opportunities-post.purpose: Offer a short assignment with the skills it needs and the skills it builds.

opportunities-insights.title: Marketplace insights
opportunities-insights.purpose: HR oversight: aggregate take-up and outcomes, suppressed below 10 people.

opportunity.title: Opportunity
opportunity.purpose: One opportunity, your match and how to apply.

rotations.title: Rotations and job shadowing
rotations.purpose: Structured rotation programmes (GDP, GPO, DNT, cross-functional and leadership) with skill objectives signed off by the host, and 1 to 5 day job shadowing.

rotations-my.title: My rotation
rotations-my.purpose: Your placement plan: hosts, objectives, the mid-point check-in, host sign-off and the skills evidence it adds to your passport; your shadowing requests.

rotations-shadow.title: Job shadowing
rotations-shadow.purpose: Ask to shadow a colleague for 1 to 5 days, with the consent of the host and your line manager, or offer to host.

rotations-host.title: Host desk
rotations-host.purpose: Placements you host or sign off, mid-point check-ins due, and shadowing requests waiting for your consent.

rotations-board.title: Rotation programme board
rotations-board.purpose: Cohort progress, objectives met and check-ins for HR programme owners; groups under 10 people are suppressed.

rotations-design.title: Design rotation programmes
rotations-design.purpose: HR programme owners design rotation templates, create cohorts and enrol people.

rotation-programme.title: Rotation programme
rotation-programme.purpose: One programme: placement sequence, host role cards, durations, skill objectives and sources.

reserve.title: Alumni and expert reserve
reserve.purpose: Retired experts and ended partner secondees who opted in to help with short mentoring, knowledge-capture interviews, guest instruction or reviews, without a re-hire.

reserve-me.title: My reserve membership
reserve-me.purpose: Join the reserve with your consent, see HR-approved requests matched to your frozen skills, and withdraw at any time.

reserve-request.title: Request reserve support
reserve-request.purpose: Managers ask the reserve for short help; HR approves the request before any alumnus sees it.

reserve-desk.title: HR reserve desk
reserve-desk.purpose: HR approves reserve requests and engagements, shortlists members, keeps the registry and the erasure schedule.

opportunities-future.title: Future-skills gigs
opportunities-future.purpose: Short gigs in five future-skills channels, ranked for you, with a time envelope your line manager approves once.

opportunities-envelope.title: My time envelope
opportunities-envelope.purpose: Ask once for a share of your time for future-skills gigs this quarter or next; gigs inside it need no per-gig release.

opportunities-envelopes.title: Team time envelopes
opportunities-envelopes.purpose: Approve or decline your reports' time envelopes once and see how much of each is used.

rotations-future.title: Future-role rotations
rotations-future.purpose: Rotation programmes aimed at future roles: digital twin, data office and the ADVANCE study team (career level only).

secondments.title: External secondments
secondments.purpose: Secondments to the IAEA, partner utilities, vendors, universities and research centres, with a return-and-transfer obligation.

secondments-desk.title: Secondment desk (HR)
secondments-desk.purpose: Plan, close and cancel external secondments; closing on return creates the knowledge-capture session.

flagHint.emirati_development: Shown on the card. It does not change anyone's match score.
flagHint.knowledge_transfer: Exposure to experts ahead of the 2030 handover.
flagHint.new_joiner_friendly: No prior experience of the area needed.

next.applied: Your line manager has been asked to release you for this work.
next.released: You are released. The poster will now decide on selection.
next.declined_release: Your line manager declined the release this time. You can apply for other opportunities.
next.selected: You are selected. When the work is done, the poster signs off what you demonstrated.
next.not_selected: You were not selected this time.
next.completed: Signed off. The skills you demonstrated are now evidence in your skills passport.

reasons.fit: {pct}% skills match: you meet {have} of {total} needed skills
reasons.stretch: Stretch: {skill} is at level {level}, the work needs {need}
reasons.open: No prerequisites: open to everyone eligible
reasons.gap_current: Builds {skill} from level {from} towards {to}, a gap in your current role
reasons.gap_target: Builds {skill} from level {from} towards {to}, needed for {role}
reasons.new_skill: Adds a new skill to your profile: {skill}
reasons.target: Works on {n} skills your target role {role} needs
reasons.not_eligible: Open to other job families, so you cannot apply
reasons.res_pref_no: Has not listed {kind} as a preferred engagement

market.intro: Short stretch assignments across the plant and the company, ranked by how well they fit your skills and where you want to go. Every match explains itself.
market.statSoonSub: Apply early: your manager releases first
market.profileSkills: {n} skills in your passport feed the match
market.how: How the match works: {s}% how well your skills cover the needed skills (each needed at level {need}), {d}% how much the work builds skills you are missing for your role or target role, {g}% fit with your target role. Nationality is never used.
market.topPicksSub: The best matches you have not applied for yet
market.noneBody: Clear a filter, or save your search and check back: new opportunities are posted every week.
market.fairBody: Every opportunity is visible to every eligible employee. Your line manager releases you before the poster can select you, and the poster can never release their own applicants. Security, cyber, safeguards and protected-area work is never listed here.

f.eligible: Only ones I can apply for

detail.siteNote: Site work takes place outside the protected area. Any site induction is arranged by the host.
detail.needSub: Each needed skill is expected at level {need} (Practitioner). A stretch is fine: say how you will close it in your note.
detail.gainSub: When the poster signs off your work, each skill you demonstrated becomes on-the-job evidence in your skills passport.
detail.closesGap: Closes a gap: level {from} now, level {to} needed
detail.newSkill: A new skill for your profile
detail.deepens: Deepens a skill you hold at level {lv}
detail.pipelineSub: You posted this opportunity. Select released applicants and sign off outcomes.
detail.targetNote: Development value uses your current role and your next step, {role}.
detail.skipNote: Your line manager posted this opportunity, so their own manager decides on the release.
detail.flow4: Your outcome is signed off into your passport
detail.closed: This opportunity is not taking applications.
detail.notEligible: This opportunity is open to other job families.
detail.note: Note to your line manager and the poster (optional)
detail.noteHint: Why you are interested and how you will fit it around your work. Up to 500 characters.
detail.releaseBody: Your line manager is asked to release you for the hours shown. The poster can only select you after that release.
detail.mirrorBody: Kafa'a records development evidence from signed-off work. It does not qualify, certify or license anyone; qualification and FANR licensing stay with the licensee's systems.
detail.gateLocked: Open to holders of a strategic credential
detail.gateLockedBody: This gig names a strategic-tier micro-credential. Earn one of these to apply:
detail.gateUnlockedBody: You hold a strategic-tier micro-credential this gig names:

my.intro: Every application, from your line manager's release to the poster's sign-off.
my.noneSaved: You have not saved any opportunities
my.evidenceTitle: Skills evidence from your signed-off work
my.withdrawBody: Your line manager and the poster will see that you withdrew. If you were selected, your place is released for someone else.

manage.intro: Release your people for development, choose applicants for your postings and sign off what they demonstrated.
manage.statReleaseSub: Your people waiting for your decision
manage.statSignSub: Selected people whose outcome you sign off
manage.makerBody: The person who posts an opportunity never releases an applicant. When you post work and one of your own team applies, their release goes to your line manager instead.
manage.noReleaseBody: When someone you manage applies for an opportunity, it appears here.
manage.noPostings: You have not posted any opportunities
manage.skipLevel: You decide because their line manager posted this opportunity
manage.releaseBody: You agree they can spend about {h} hours a week on this work for the dates shown. The poster then decides on selection.
manage.declineBody: The applicant sees your reason. Be specific, for example about shift cover or timing.
manage.awaitingRelease: Waiting for the line manager's release
manage.releaseFirst: The line manager must release them first
manage.selectBody: They take one place on this opportunity. The selection is recorded in the NEXUS evidence ledger.
manage.notSelectBody: The applicant is told they were not selected this time.
manage.evidenceWritten: {n} skills evidence rows added to their passport
manage.openBody: It becomes visible in the marketplace to every eligible employee.
manage.closeBody: It stops taking applications. Applicants still waiting for release or selection are told it closed.

signoff.title: Sign off the outcome for {name}
signoff.body: Rate each skill the person demonstrated on this work. Each rated skill becomes on-the-job evidence (basis: evidenced) in their skills passport.
signoff.mirrorBody: This records development evidence only, at most level 3. Task qualification sign-offs stay in the qualification system.

post.intro: Offer a short piece of real work. Say what skills it needs and what it builds; the marketplace matches it to people and explains why.
post.summaryHint: 20 to 1,000 characters: the work, who it is with, what people learn.
post.restricted: Security, cyber, safeguards and protected-area work cannot be posted here.
post.neededHint: Up to six. Leave empty if anyone can start.
post.gainedHint: One to six. These are signed off as evidence at the end.
post.familiesHint: Leave all unticked to open it to every family.
post.flowBody: Applicants' line managers release them first. You then select, and at the end you sign off the skills each person demonstrated.
post.openBody: It becomes visible to every eligible employee and is ranked against their skills.
post.draftBody: Only you can see a draft. Publish it from the release and selection desk.

insights.intro: How the marketplace is used and what it develops. Counts only: no names, and any group under 10 people is suppressed.
insights.noAccess: Marketplace aggregates are for HR, managers and auditors
insights.ktSub: Open opportunities ahead of the 2030 handover
insights.byFamilySub: Families with fewer than {n} applicants are suppressed.
insights.noteBody: The marketplace measures skills gained through signed-off work, not retention. Evidence that rotation alone reduces turnover is mixed, so no retention claim is made here.

programme.placementsSub: Each placement has a host role card and skill objectives that the host signs off. Your current level is shown against each target.
programme.fitSub: {n} of {total} objectives would grow a skill above your current level.
programme.navigator: Change it in the Career Navigator
programme.howBody: The HR programme owner enrols you with your line manager. At the mid-point you or your host record a check-in; at the end the host signs off each objective, which adds on-the-job evidence to your skills passport. If your host is also your line manager, their own manager signs off (maker-checker).

reasons.closure: {n} of {total} objectives would grow a skill above your current level
reasons.target: Works on {n} skills your target role {role} needs
reasons.consolidate: You already meet every objective: this would consolidate, not stretch
reasons.host_wanted: Offers {n} of the {total} skills you picked
reasons.host_growth: You could grow {skill} (you are at level {level})
reasons.host_refresh: You already hold these skills at level 2 or above: a refresher
reasons.host_target: {n} of the skills on offer are needed for {role}
reasons.host_cross: A look at another job family: {family}
reasons.host_days: Hosts up to {n} days a month

common.siteHint: Plant-based work: site induction is arranged by the host. Kafa'a shows no access details.
common.mirrorBody: Rotation and shadowing sign-offs are on-the-job development evidence in Kafa'a (at most level 3). They are not qualification sign-offs, licences or FANR authorisations, which stay in the licensee's systems. People and cohorts here are synthetic.

hub.intro: Structured rotations with clear objectives and a host who signs them off, plus short job shadowing. Programmes are ranked by how much they would grow your skills, and every ranking explains itself.
hub.statMineNone: You are not on a rotation
hub.shadowApproved: You also have approved shadowing coming up.
hub.programmesSub: Ranked for you against your target role ({role}).
hub.enrolNote: Enrolment is made by the HR programme owner with your line manager. Talk to your manager if a programme fits your development plan.
hub.shadowSub: Suggested hosts who offer skills you want to grow. Shadowing needs your host's and your line manager's consent.

my.intro: Your placement plan with the host, objectives and dates of each placement, the mid-point check-in and the host sign-off that adds evidence to your skills passport.
my.noPlan: You are not on a rotation programme
my.noPlanBody: Browse the programmes and talk to your line manager; HR enrols you in a cohort.
my.noShadowBody: Pick a host in the directory and ask for 1 to 5 days.
my.signedOff: Signed off on {d}: {n} skills evidence rows added to your passport
my.awaitingSignoff: The placement has ended and is waiting for the host sign-off.
my.overdueNoCheckin: The placement has ended without a mid-point check-in: record it so the host can sign off.
my.withdrawBody: The host and your line manager are told the request is withdrawn. You can ask again later.

checkin.title: Mid-point check-in: {team}
checkin.body: Give a status for every objective and a short note. The check-in is recorded once, by you or your host, and the host needs it before signing off.
checkin.note: Note (what is going well, what needs support)

signoff.title: Sign off placement: {name}
signoff.body: Rate each objective for {team}. Each rated skill is recorded as on-the-job evidence (basis "evidenced") and the person's skills passport is recomputed.
signoff.levels: Objectives ({met} of {total} met at these levels)
signoff.mirror: This records development evidence in Kafa'a only. It is not a qualification sign-off and grants no authorisation.

host.intro: Placements you host and sign off, check-ins that are due, and shadowing requests that need your consent. If you are both host and line manager, your own manager signs off (maker-checker).
host.statSignSub: {n} placements route their sign-off to you
host.statCheckinsSub: past the mid-point without a check-in
host.makerBody: Nobody signs off their own placement. When the host is also the person's line manager, the sign-off goes to the host's own line manager, and the system refuses it otherwise.
host.noSignBody: Placements appear here once they start; sign-off opens after the mid-point check-in.
host.noHosting: You are not hosting any placement
host.skipYou: You sign off because the host is this person's line manager (maker-checker).
host.hostIsLm: You host and line-manage this person, so your own manager signs off.
host.consentBody: The request is approved once both the host and the line manager consent.
host.consentBothBody: You are both host and line manager, so your consent approves the request.
host.declineBody: The requester sees your reason and can ask again later.
host.completeBody: Confirming records on-the-job evidence at level 1 for each skill shadowed and updates the person's skills passport.
host.completeNote: What did they see and do?

shadow.intro: Shadow a colleague for 1 to 5 days to see their work first hand. Hosts opt in; every request needs the host's and your line manager's consent. Security, cyber and safeguards work is never shadowed.
shadow.directorySub: Ranked by the skills you could grow and your target role ({role}).
shadow.pickFirstBody: Pick a host in the directory to write your request.
shadow.purpose: What do you want to learn?
shadow.purposeHint: One or two sentences for your host and line manager
shadow.consentNote: Your host and your line manager both consent before it is approved. You have {n} open requests (at most 3).
shadow.confirmBody: {n} days from {d}. Your host and your line manager are notified.
shadow.offerOn: You are listed as a host for {n} skills.
shadow.offerOff: Share your work: list yourself as a shadowing host for the skills you can show.
shadow.daysMonth: Days a month you can host
shadow.restrictedHost: Security, cyber and safeguards roles are shown as career paths only, so they cannot host shadowing.
shadow.rulesBody: Shadowing lasts 1 to 5 days on skills the host offers. The host and your line manager both consent; if they are the same person one consent counts for both. After the visit the host confirms it took place, which records level-1 on-the-job evidence. Plant-based hosts show only "site induction required"; Kafa'a holds no access details.

board.intro: Cohort progress for HR programme owners: placements signed off, objectives met and mid-point check-ins. Counts only; any cohort or family with fewer than 10 people is suppressed.
board.noAccess: The programme board is for HR programme owners and auditors
board.evidenceSub: ojt evidence written by host sign-off
board.cohortsSub: Tiles with fewer than {n} people are suppressed.
board.byFamilySub: Families with fewer than {n} people are suppressed and left out of the chart.
board.noteBody: Kafa'a measures skills gained and objectives met, not retention: evidence that rotation alone reduces turnover is mixed. Numbers come from synthetic cohorts and never name a person.

design.intro: Design rotation programmes: the placement sequence, host role cards, durations and skill objectives. Create cohorts and enrol people; each enrolment builds the person's placement plan and sign-off route.
design.rulesBody: Placements must add up to the programme duration. Security, cyber and safeguards placements are career-path only and are refused. Every save is audited.
design.cohortBody: The cohort is listed for staff and can take enrolments.
design.total: Placements add up to {n} months (programme {min} to {max})
design.eligibleHint: None selected: open to all job families.
design.sources: Sources for public facts (such as the programme duration)
design.restricted: Security, cyber and safeguards families and skills are not offered: they appear as career paths only.

enrol.title: Enrol a person
enrol.inactive: Publish the programme before enrolling people.
enrol.noAccess: Only HR programme owners can enrol people
enrol.routing: Each placement is signed off by its host, or by the host's line manager when the host is the person's own line manager.
enrol.confirmBody: {name} gets {n} placements starting {d}. The person and the first host are notified, and the enrolment is recorded in the evidence ledger.

res.handoffNote: Kafa'a records only that an engagement was handed to HR. Contracts, payment and contact details stay outside Kafa'a.

engHint.mentor: Regular conversations with one or two people
engHint.capture_interview: A recorded, structured interview for the knowledge base
engHint.instructor: Co-teach a session with the training team
engHint.reviewer: Review a document, package or programme

hub.intro: When experts retire or a partner secondment ends, the link does not have to end. People who opt in stay available for short mentoring, knowledge-capture interviews, guest instruction and reviews. HR approves every request and arranges every engagement.
hub.statExpertsSub: Members who opted into the expert finder
hub.statSkillsSub: Distinct skills in their frozen snapshots
hub.howSub: Retired-expert reserves are a standard knowledge-loss mitigation in IAEA knowledge loss risk management.

optin.title: Opt in with consent
optin.body: Choose your availability, hours and the kinds of help you offer. Your skills are frozen from your skills passport when you join. You can withdraw at any time.

request.title: A manager asks, HR approves
request.body: Managers describe a short need and the skills it takes. HR approves the request before any alumnus sees it.

handoff.title: Interest, then handed to HR
handoff.body: Members see approved requests matched to their skills and say they are interested. HR approves and arranges the engagement outside Kafa'a.

hub.expertsSub: Only members who opted into the expert finder appear here. There are no contact details: ask through a reserve request and HR makes the contact.
hub.noExperts: No alumni have opted into the expert finder yet
hub.noExpertsBody: Members choose whether staff can find them. Withdrawing consent hides a member at once.
hub.searchExperts: Search by skill, role or name
hub.contactViaHr: Contact goes through HR: Kafa'a stores no contact details.
hub.askReserve: Need one of these experts? Request reserve support
hub.storiesSub: Stories are published only with the alumnus's consent. All people and events in this demo are synthetic.
hub.privacyBody: Membership is opt-in. Withdrawing consent hides a member everywhere at once (expert finder, HR shortlists and stories), ends open engagements and schedules erasure of the record after six months. Kafa'a stores no contact data, contract or payment.

me.intro: Your consent, your availability and the skills you are known for. Alumni and pre-departure members see HR-approved requests here.
me.restrictedBody: Security, cyber and safeguards roles are shown as a career path only, so they cannot join the expert reserve.
me.withdrawnBody: You withdrew your consent on {date}. You are hidden from the reserve, and your record is erased after {erase}. You can join again below.
me.boardSub: HR-approved requests, ranked by how well your frozen skills fit. You never see who posted a request, only the team.
me.noRequestsBody: HR opens requests to the reserve after approving them. You will get a notice when HR invites you.
me.interestBody: HR sees your interest and decides. If approved, HR contacts you outside Kafa'a.
me.noteHint: Up to 500 characters. Do not include phone numbers or email addresses.
me.withdrawEngBody: HR and the requesting manager are told that you withdrew. You stay in the reserve.
me.handedBody: HR approved this engagement and will contact you. Contract and payment, if any, are handled by HR outside Kafa'a.
me.frozenOn: Frozen from your skills passport on {date}. Saving your membership refreshes it.
me.withdrawText: You disappear from the expert finder, HR shortlists and stories at once. Open engagements end, and your record is erased after six months.
me.withdrawConfirmBody: You will be hidden from the reserve everywhere straight away, your open engagements end, your stories are unlisted, and your record is erased after six months. You can join again later.
me.joinIntro: Leaving soon, or want to stay useful after you leave? Join with your consent. Your skills are frozen from your skills passport today; HR approves every request before you see it.
me.headlineHint: Up to 160 characters, no contact details
me.finderLabel: Let staff find me in the expert finder
me.finderHint: Shows your name, former role, frozen skills and availability to staff. Never contact details.
me.previewSub: From your skills passport: your strongest skills, at most 12. Security skills are never included.
me.consentLabel: I consent to joining the reserve
me.consentHint: Consent version 1. You can withdraw at any time from this page.
me.joinConfirmBody: {n} skills will be frozen from your skills passport, together with your availability and preferences. Your consent is recorded in the audit log and the NEXUS ledger.

req.intro: Ask retired experts and ended partner secondees for short help. HR approves the request first, then members of the reserve see it. You see who was matched once HR hands the engagement over.
req.restricted: Security, cyber, safeguards and protected-area work is never requested from the reserve.
req.skillsHint: One to six skills from the catalogue. Members are matched on their frozen skills.
req.flowBody: HR approves or declines your request. Approved requests are shown to reserve members only, with your team but never your name. HR approves the alumni who are interested and arranges the engagement. You then confirm the outcome.
req.confirmBody: HR reviews the request before any alumnus sees it. Nothing is shared outside the reserve.
req.mineSub: Status, interest and the alumni HR handed over to you.
req.none: You have not requested reserve support yet
req.awaitingHr: Waiting for HR approval: no alumnus can see this request yet.
req.completeBody: Describe what the engagement achieved. The completion is recorded in the audit log and the NEXUS ledger.
req.closeBody: Members can no longer see it. Pending interest and invitations are declined.

desk.intro: Approve reserve requests and engagements, shortlist members with the match engine and keep the registry. You never approve your own request or an engagement that involves you.
desk.forbidden: The reserve desk is for HR
desk.ownRequest: Your own: another HR approver decides
desk.approveReqTitle: Open this request to the reserve?
desk.approveReqBody: Reserve members will see it with the poster's team (never the poster's name). Recorded in the audit log and the NEXUS ledger.
desk.declineReqBody: The manager is told why. No alumnus sees the request.
desk.noOpen: No requests are open to the reserve
desk.inviteBody: {name} sees the request on the reserve board and can accept.
desk.handoffBody: The requesting manager now sees the alumnus. HR arranges any contract, payment and contact outside Kafa'a. Recorded in the audit log and the NEXUS ledger.
desk.declineEngBody: The member stays in the reserve and is told the engagement will not go ahead.
desk.erasureSub: Members who withdrew consent: record ids and dates only. Records are erased six months after withdrawal.
desk.glanceSub: Counts of active members and approved engagements. Every cell under {n} people is suppressed.
desk.openEngNote: {n} engagements are open (invited, interested or handed to HR).
desk.noteTitle: Kafa'a is not the contract system
desk.noteBody: This desk records consent, requests and approvals only. Contracts, payment and contact details are handled by HR outside Kafa'a. All people shown are synthetic.

finderNote.title: Also in the alumni and expert reserve
finderNote.body: {n} alumni and partner experts have opted into the expert finder. Requests go through HR; no contact details are shared.
finderNote.bodySkill: {n} alumni and partner experts in the reserve list this skill in their frozen skill snapshot. Requests go through HR; no contact details are shared.

envelope.fits: Fits your time envelope ({used} of {cap} h/week used; this gig adds {hours})
envelope.over_limit: Would go over your envelope ({used} of {cap} h/week used; this gig adds {hours})
envelope.poster_is_approver: Posted by the manager who approved your envelope: the usual release applies
envelope.no_envelope: No approved time envelope covers it yet

lifecycle.emerging: {skill} is an emerging skill in the catalogue
lifecycle.growing: {skill} is a growing skill in the catalogue

fit.fits: Inside your envelope: released at once
fit.poster_is_approver: Posted by your approver: per-gig release

fitHint.fits: Your approved envelope covers this gig ({used} of {cap} h/week used before it), so your application is released at once without a per-gig release.
fitHint.over_limit: Your envelope has {used} of {cap} h/week in use; this gig would go over it, so your line manager releases this application as usual.
fitHint.poster_is_approver: The person who approved your envelope posted this gig, so the release goes through the usual maker-checker route.
fitHint.no_envelope: No approved envelope covers this gig's channel and dates; your line manager releases the application, or ask for an envelope first.
fitHint.not_future: This is not a future-skills gig, so the per-gig release applies.

post.channelHint: Pick a channel to list this as a future-skills gig. It must grow at least one future skill.

hub.intro: Short gigs that build the skills ENEC will need: ADVANCE study support, digital innovation, governed AI pilots, data clean-up and knowledge capture. Ask your line manager once for a time envelope and you can join gigs inside it without a release for each one.
hub.statFitsSub: Released at once if you apply
hub.listSub: Ranked by how much each grows future skills you do not hold yet, and whether it fits your envelope. Open "Why this?" for the reasons.
hub.empty: No open gigs in this channel right now
hub.envRunning: {pct}% of your time in {period}: up to {cap} h/week for future-skills gigs.
hub.envRule: Applications inside the envelope are released at once. Above the limit, your line manager releases each one as usual.
hub.envPending: Your request for {period} is with your line manager.
hub.envNone: Ask your line manager once for up to 20% of your time this quarter or next. You then join gigs without a release for each one.
hub.how1: You ask once: a share of your time (5 to 20%), a quarter and the channels you want.
hub.how2: Your line manager of record approves once. Nobody approves their own envelope.
hub.how3: Inside the envelope, applying to a future gig releases you at once. The poster still selects.
hub.how4: When the poster signs off the outcome, the skills evidence goes into your passport.

hr.title: Programme view (HR)
hr.sub: Counts of gigs and envelopes. People counts below {min} are suppressed. Nobody is ranked.
hr.share: Open gigs that build future skills
hr.evidenceSub: Written when a poster signs off an outcome
hr.shareLine: Share of open opportunities that build future skills
hr.shareNote: The marker shows ordinary stretch assignments that happen to grow a future skill, measured on the same data.
hr.noRank: This view never lists or ranks people. Envelope decisions stay between each person and their line manager.

env.intro: Ask your line manager once for a share of your working time for future-skills gigs. While the envelope runs, gigs inside it need no per-gig release.
env.noneBody: Use the form to ask for one. Your line manager decides once for the whole quarter.
env.withdrawBody: New applications will need a per-gig release again. Gigs already released stay as they are.
env.allSetBody: You already have an envelope requested or approved for this quarter and the next.
env.reasonHint: One or two sentences for your line manager (10 to 400 characters).
env.confirmBody: Your line manager will be asked to approve {pct}% of your time (up to {h} h/week) for future-skills gigs in {period}.

team.intro: Approve a time envelope once instead of releasing your report for every gig. You see each approved envelope's use; selection and sign-off stay with the gig poster.
team.noneBody: When someone you manage asks for a time envelope, it appears here.
team.pendingDesc: You decide once for the quarter. Declining needs a reason.
team.approveBody: {pct}% of their time (up to {h} h/week) in {period}. Applications to future gigs inside it will be released at once; you are recorded as the approver in the evidence ledger.
team.declineBody: They will see your reason and can ask again later.
team.usageDesc: Hours per week taken by live future gigs (applied, released or selected).
team.rule: Only the line manager of record approves, never the person themselves. If you post a gig yourself, your report's application to it still needs the usual release.

msg.not_signed_in: Sign in to use future-skills gigs
msg.forbidden_request: Only staff can ask for a time envelope
msg.invalid_pct: Choose 5, 10, 15 or 20 % of your working time
msg.invalid_period: Choose this quarter or the next one
msg.invalid_channels: Choose one or more of the five future-skills channels
msg.invalid_reason: Say in a sentence why you want the time (10 to 400 characters)
msg.duplicate: You already have a time envelope requested or approved for this quarter
msg.no_line_manager: No line manager is recorded for you; ask HR to update your record
msg.maker_checker: You cannot approve your own time envelope
msg.forbidden_decide: Only your line manager approves your time envelope
msg.not_requested: This time envelope is not waiting for a decision
msg.decline_reason: Give a reason when you decline
msg.forbidden_withdraw: Only the person who asked can withdraw a time envelope
msg.not_withdrawable: This time envelope can no longer be withdrawn
msg.channel_needs_future_skill: A future-skills gig must grow at least one future skill from the catalogue

rot.intro: Rotation programmes aimed at roles ENEC may need: each prepares for one or more concept roles from the career map. ADVANCE study is career-level only: study work, no deployment decision implied.
rot.statTracksSub: Digital twin, data office, ADVANCE study
rot.none: No future-role programme is published yet
rot.draftsSub: Visible to their programme owner only
rot.noDeployment: Study work only: no deployment decision is implied, and nothing here plans a location or staffing numbers.
rot.securityTitle: Security work stays at career level
rot.security: Security, cyber and safeguards roles are never part of a rotation or a secondment. Their career paths are shown in the career map only.
rot.tagTitle: Mark a programme as a future-role rotation
rot.tagIntro: Programme owners link a rotation to a future track and up to four concept roles. Security, cyber and safeguards roles are refused.
rot.tagBody: Staff will see this programme among the future-role rotations.
rot.tagAdvance: ADVANCE study rotations are marked career-level only: no deployment decision implied, no location or staffing numbers.

page.intro: Outbound secondments to the IAEA, partner utilities, vendors, universities and research centres. Each has objectives tied to skills, a host supervisor role and an obligation to share what you learned within 60 days of return.
page.mineSub: Host, objectives, dates and your return-and-transfer obligation.
page.noneMineBody: HR plans secondments with your line manager. Future-role rotations and gigs are open to you now.
page.teamSub: People you manage. You run the knowledge-capture session when they return.
page.how1: HR plans the secondment with objectives tied to catalogue skills and a host supervisor (a role, never a name).
page.how2: While you are away, your line manager stays your contact at ENEC.
page.how3: On return HR closes the secondment and records which objectives were met.
page.how4: Closing creates a knowledge-capture session with your line manager, due within 60 days of your return.
page.security: Security, cyber and safeguards staff, skills and roles are never offered a secondment or rotation; the system refuses and records the attempt.

f.countryHint: Two-letter code, for example AE, KR, AT
f.supervisorHint: A role such as "Section head (host role)", never a name

transfer.due: Share what you learned by {due}. The session is planned for {planned}.
transfer.overdue: The knowledge-capture session was due by {due} and has not been held yet.
transfer.done: Done: the knowledge-capture session was held. Due date was {due}.

desk.intro: Plan external secondments, close them on return (this creates the knowledge-capture session, due within 60 days) or cancel them. Every action is recorded; plans and returns also go to the evidence ledger.
desk.noAccessBody: The secondment desk is for HR analysts, the CHCO office and auditors.
desk.statReturnDueSub: Ended and waiting to be closed
desk.planBody: The person and their line manager are notified, and the plan is recorded in the evidence ledger.
desk.transferBody: Closing on return creates a structured knowledge-capture session with the person's line manager, due within 60 days of the return date. The return is recorded in the evidence ledger.
desk.cancelBody: The person is told the secondment is cancelled, with your reason.

msg.forbidden_hr: Only HR (the CHCO office and HR analysts) plans and closes secondments
msg.restricted: Security, cyber and safeguards work is career-path only and is never offered as a secondment or rotation
msg.invalid_host_kind: Choose the IAEA, a partner utility, a vendor, a university or a research centre
msg.invalid_host: Give the host in English and Arabic (3 to 120 characters) and a two-letter country code
msg.invalid_supervisor: Name the host supervisor by role in English and Arabic (3 to 120 characters), never by name
msg.invalid_objectives: Give one to five objectives, each tied to a catalogue skill at level 1 to 3, in English and Arabic (5 to 200 characters)
msg.invalid_dates: Start between today and twelve months from now, for 1 to 24 months
msg.invalid_role: Choose a current or concept role from the career map
msg.overlap: This person already has a secondment planned for these dates
msg.no_line_manager: No line manager is recorded for this person; update their record first
msg.invalid_return: Record a return date between the start of the secondment and today, at most 30 days ago
msg.invalid_outcome: Describe the outcome in at least one sentence (10 to 1,000 characters)
msg.invalid_met: Say for every objective whether it was met
msg.cancel_reason: Give a reason when you cancel
msg.no_interviewer: Nobody can run the knowledge-capture session; record a line manager for this person first
msg.forbidden_owner: Only HR programme owners and the training manager manage rotation programmes
msg.invalid_roles: Choose up to four current or concept roles (never security, cyber or safeguards roles)
